/-!
# Conjecture 7.38

by O. V. Mel'nikov

A *variety of profinite groups* is a non-empty class of profinite groups closed under
taking subgroups, factor-groups, and Tikhonov products. A subvariety $\mathfrak{V}$ of the
variety $\mathfrak{N}$ of all pronilpotent groups is said to be *(locally) nilpotent* if all
(finitely generated) groups in $\mathfrak{V}$ are nilpotent.

a) Is it true that any non-nilpotent subvariety of $\mathfrak{N}$ contains a non-nilpotent
locally nilpotent subvariety?

b) The same problem for the variety of all pro-$p$-groups (for a given prime $p$).

Here, as usual for profinite groups, "subgroups" are closed subgroups, "factor-groups" are
quotients by closed normal subgroups (equivalently, images under continuous surjective
homomorphisms onto profinite groups), "Tikhonov products" are arbitrary direct products with
the product topology, and "finitely generated" means topologically finitely generated.
"Nilpotent" refers to the underlying abstract group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A profinite group $G$ is *topologically finitely generated* if some finite subset of $G$
generates a dense subgroup of $G$.

nilpotent, i.e. $G / N$ is nilpotent for every open normal subgroup $N$ of $G$. Equivalently,

A profinite group $G$ is a *pro-$p$ group* if all of its finite continuous quotients are

structure IsVariety (V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop where
  /-- The class is non-empty. -/
  nonempty : V.Nonempty
  /-- The class is closed under taking closed subgroups. -/
  closedSubgroup_mem : ∀ G ∈ V, ∀ H : ClosedSubgroup G, ProfiniteGrp.ofClosedSubgroup H ∈ V
  /-- The class is closed under taking factor-groups, i.e. continuous homomorphic images. -/
  mem_of_surjective : ∀ G ∈ V, ∀ (H : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (f : G →ₜ* H),
    Function.Surjective f → H ∈ V
  /-- The class is closed under Tikhonov products, i.e. arbitrary direct products with the
  product topology. -/
  pi_mem : ∀ {ι : Type u} (G : ι → ProfiniteGrp.{u}), (∀ i, G i ∈ V) → ProfiniteGrp.pi G ∈ V
blocks.docstring:
A *variety of profinite groups* is a non-empty class $\mathfrak{V}$ of profinite groups
that is closed under taking closed subgroups, factor-groups, and Tikhonov products.

Factor-groups are formalised as images under continuous surjective homomorphisms onto
profinite groups; these are exactly the quotients $G / N$ by closed normal subgroups $N$, up to
topological isomorphism. In particular, a variety is closed under topological isomorphism.

justification.closest_existing_considered: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty / closure under limits (too abstract and not matching subgroup/quotient closure); Mathlib has no abstract group varieties either.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.38».IsVariety
justification.why_needed: No Mathlib/repo notion of a variety of (profinite) groups; needed the closure properties under closed subgroups, continuous homomorphic images and Tikhonov products.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: for every variety V of profinite groups (non-empty class closed under closed subgroups, quotients by closed normal subgroups, and arbitrary Tikhonov/direct products) consisting of pronilpotent groups and containing a non-nilpotent group, does V contain a subvariety W that still has a non-nilpotent member but in which every topologically finitely generated group is nilpotent; 'subgroups' means closed subgroups and 'finitely generated' means topologically finitely generated, while 'nilpotent' is nilpotency of the underlying abstract group (equivalently bounded class for profinite groups).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same correct logical shape: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ V (variety, all members pronilpotent, not all members nilpotent), ∃ W ⊆ V with W a variety ∧ W non-nilpotent ∧ every topologically f.g. member of W nilpotent (conjunction, not implication, under the existential; hypotheses satisfiable and the conclusion non-trivial). c06 was chosen as the base because it is the most literal and best documented: closure under subgroups is stated via `ClosedSubgroup`/`ProfiniteGrp.ofClosedSubgroup` (closed subgroups, as the notes require) rather than the equivalent-but-indirect injective-hom encodings of c01/c05/c07/c08; factor-groups are continuous surjective images `G →ₜ* H` (Mathlib has no ProfiniteGrp structure on G ⧸ N; the encoding is equivalent for compact Hausdorff groups and gives the implicit isomorphism-closure of a class); Tikhonov products via `ProfiniteGrp.pi` over arbitrary index types; pronilpotent = every quotient by an open normal subgroup is nilpotent (the standard finite-continuous-quotient characterization); topological finite generation = a finite set generates a dense subgroup; nilpotency = `Group.IsNilpotent` of the underlying group. The theorem is at universe 0, matching the repository's `Type` convention. I added c03's `isVariety_univ` sanity test (adapted to c06's field names) alongside c06's three API lemmas, per the CONTRIBUTING request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.38

by O. V. Mel'nikov

A *variety of profinite groups* is a non-empty class of profinite groups closed under
taking subgroups, factor-groups, and Tikhonov products. A subvariety $\mathfrak{V}$ of the
variety $\mathfrak{N}$ of all pronilpotent groups is said to be *(locally) nilpotent* if all
(finitely generated) groups in $\mathfrak{V}$ are nilpotent.

Here, as usual for profinite groups, "subgroups" are closed subgroups, "factor-groups" are
quotients by closed normal subgroups (equivalently, images under continuous surjective
homomorphisms onto profinite groups), "Tikhonov products" are arbitrary direct products with
the product topology, and "finitely generated" means topologically finitely generated.
"Nilpotent" refers to the underlying abstract group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.38»

universe u

/-- A profinite group $G$ is *topologically finitely generated* if some finite subset of $G$
generates a dense subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset G, (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

/-- A profinite group $G$ is *pronilpotent* if all of its finite continuous quotients are
nilpotent, i.e. $G / N$ is nilpotent for every open normal subgroup $N$ of $G$. Equivalently,
$G$ is an inverse limit of finite nilpotent groups. -/
def IsPronilpotent (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, Group.IsNilpotent (G ⧸ N.toSubgroup)

/-- A profinite group $G$ is a *pro-$p$ group* if all of its finite continuous quotients are
$p$-groups, i.e. $G / N$ is a $p$-group for every open normal subgroup $N$ of $G$. Equivalently,
$G$ is an inverse limit of finite $p$-groups. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, IsPGroup p (G ⧸ N.toSubgroup)

/-- A *variety of profinite groups* is a non-empty class $\mathfrak{V}$ of profinite groups
that is closed under taking closed subgroups, factor-groups, and Tikhonov products.

Factor-groups are formalised as images under continuous surjective homomorphisms onto
profinite groups; these are exactly the quotients $G / N$ by closed normal subgroups $N$, up to
topological isomorphism. In particular, a variety is closed under topological isomorphism. -/
structure IsVariety (V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop where
  /-- The class is non-empty. -/
  nonempty : V.Nonempty
  /-- The class is closed under taking closed subgroups. -/
  closedSubgroup_mem : ∀ G ∈ V, ∀ H : ClosedSubgroup G, ProfiniteGrp.ofClosedSubgroup H ∈ V
  /-- The class is closed under taking factor-groups, i.e. continuous homomorphic images. -/
  mem_of_surjective : ∀ G ∈ V, ∀ (H : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (f : G →ₜ* H),
    Function.Surjective f → H ∈ V
  /-- The class is closed under Tikhonov products, i.e. arbitrary direct products with the
  product topology. -/
  pi_mem : ∀ {ι : Type u} (G : ι → ProfiniteGrp.{u}), (∀ i, G i ∈ V) → ProfiniteGrp.pi G ∈ V

/-- A class $\mathfrak{V}$ of profinite groups is *nilpotent* if all groups in $\mathfrak{V}$
are nilpotent. -/
def IsNilpotentClass (V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ G ∈ V, Group.IsNilpotent G

/-- A class $\mathfrak{V}$ of profinite groups is *locally nilpotent* if all (topologically)
finitely generated groups in $\mathfrak{V}$ are nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotentClass (V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ G ∈ V, IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G → Group.IsNilpotent G

/-- The class of all profinite groups is a variety. -/
@[category test, AMS 20 22]
theorem isVariety_univ : IsVariety (Set.univ : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) where
  nonempty := ⟨.of PUnit, trivial⟩
  closedSubgroup_mem _ _ _ := trivial
  mem_of_surjective _ _ _ _ _ := trivial
  pi_mem _ _ := trivial

/-- A nilpotent class of profinite groups is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem IsNilpotentClass.isLocallyNilpotentClass {V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}}
    (hV : IsNilpotentClass V) : IsLocallyNilpotentClass V :=
  fun G hG _ => hV G hG

/-- A nilpotent profinite group is pronilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem IsPronilpotent.of_isNilpotent (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsPronilpotent G :=
  fun _ => inferInstance

/-- A pro-$p$ group (for a prime $p$) is pronilpotent, so the variety of all pro-$p$ groups is
a subvariety of the variety $\mathfrak{N}$ of all pronilpotent groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem IsProP.isPronilpotent {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}} (hG : IsProP p G) :
    IsPronilpotent G :=
  fun N => (hG N).isNilpotent

/--
Is it true that any non-nilpotent subvariety $\mathfrak{V}$ of the variety $\mathfrak{N}$ of all
pronilpotent groups contains a non-nilpotent locally nilpotent subvariety $\mathfrak{W}$?

That is: for every variety $\mathfrak{V}$ of profinite groups consisting of pronilpotent groups
and containing a non-nilpotent group, is there a variety $\mathfrak{W} \subseteq \mathfrak{V}$
which contains a non-nilpotent group but in which every topologically finitely generated group
is nilpotent?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«7.38».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}, IsVariety V → (∀ G ∈ V, IsPronilpotent G) →
      ¬ IsNilpotentClass V →
      ∃ W ⊆ V, IsVariety W ∧ ¬ IsNilpotentClass W ∧ IsLocallyNilpotentClass W := by
  sorry

/--
The same problem for the variety of all pro-$p$-groups (for a given prime $p$): is it true
that, for every prime $p$, any non-nilpotent subvariety $\mathfrak{V}$ of the variety of all
pro-$p$ groups contains a non-nilpotent locally nilpotent subvariety $\mathfrak{W}$?

@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«7.38».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime →
      ∀ V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}, IsVariety V → (∀ G ∈ V, IsProP p G) →
        ¬ IsNilpotentClass V →
        ∃ W ⊆ V, IsVariety W ∧ ¬ IsNilpotentClass W ∧ IsLocallyNilpotentClass W := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.38»

items: Profinite groups are modelled by Mathlib's bundled `ProfiniteGrp` (compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological groups); a 'class of profinite groups' is a `Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}` (universe 0, mirroring the repository's use of `Type` in other Kourovka files); Tikhonov products are indexed by types in `Type 0`.
'Closed under subgroups' is formalised as closure under closed subgroups via `ProfiniteGrp.ofClosedSubgroup` (abstract subgroups of profinite groups are not profinite).

'Closed under factor-groups' is formalised as closure under images of continuous surjective homomorphisms `G →ₜ* H` onto profinite groups `H`. Mathlib has no instance making `G ⧸ N` totally disconnected for closed normal `N`, and this formulation is mathematically equivalent (a continuous surjection between profinite groups is a quotient map, so H ≅ G/ker f; conversely G/N is profinite). It also makes varieties closed under topological isomorphism, as classes of groups are always assumed to be.

'Pronilpotent' is defined as: G ⧸ N is nilpotent for every open normal subgroup N (all finite continuous quotients nilpotent). This is a standard characterisation equivalent to 'inverse limit of finite nilpotent groups' (Ribes–Zalesskii, Prop. 2.1.3). Likewise 'pro-p' is defined as: G ⧸ N is a p-group for every open normal N, with p.Prime assumed in the theorem.
'Nilpotent' for a profinite group is `Group.IsNilpotent` of the underlying abstract group, per the decomposition notes.

'Finitely generated' is topologically finitely generated: some finite subset generates a dense subgroup (`(Subgroup.closure S).topologicalClosure = ⊤`). Abstract finite generation would make every subvariety of N trivially locally nilpotent, so this is the only sensible reading.

'Non-nilpotent subvariety' is `¬ IsNilpotentClass V`, i.e. (classically) V contains a non-nilpotent group; 'subvariety of N' is `IsVariety V ∧ ∀ G ∈ V, IsPronilpotent G`; 'contains a subvariety W' is `∃ W ⊆ V, IsVariety W ∧ …`.
In part b) the prime p is universally quantified inside the `answer(sorry) ↔ …` as instructed by the decomposition notes (rather than being a theorem parameter).

Three short `@[category API]` lemmas are included as tests of the definitions: nilpotent class ⇒ locally nilpotent class; nilpotent profinite group ⇒ pronilpotent; pro-p (p prime) ⇒ pronilpotent (so b) is indeed a special case of a)).

reviewer_notes: Every candidate compiled and was logically faithful; differences were only in modeling style, so the final file is c06's declarations plus c03's `isVariety_univ` test. Modeling choices a human should be aware of: (1) 'factor-groups' are encoded as continuous surjective homomorphic images between profinite groups rather than literal quotients G ⧸ N by closed normal N (Mathlib lacks a ProfiniteGrp instance for such quotients); for profinite groups this is equivalent up to topological isomorphism and additionally forces the class to be isomorphism-closed, which the informal notion of a 'class of groups' presupposes. (2) 'Pronilpotent'/'pro-p' are defined via quotients by open normal subgroups, the standard characterization of inverse limits of finite nilpotent / finite p-groups. (3) Classes live in `Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}` with Tikhonov products indexed by `Type 0`, following the repository's `Type` convention; the definitions themselves are universe polymorphic. (4) 'Subvariety' is not required to be proper (the notebook does not say proper). (5) Ambiguity: in part b) 'for a given prime p' is read as a universal quantifier placed after answer(sorry), as the decomposition table instructs; the alternative reading (p as a theorem parameter with a possibly p-dependent answer) is also defensible, and several candidates (c02, c04) flagged this. Under the universal reading a positive answer to a) implies a positive answer to b).
statement:
A variety of profinite groups is a non-empty class of profinite groups closed under taking subgroups, factor-groups, and Tikhonov products. A subvariety ${\goth V}$ of the variety ${\goth N}$ of all pronilpotent groups is said to be $($locally$)$ nilpotent if all (finitely generated) groups in ${\goth V}$ are nilpotent.

a) Is it true that any non-nilpotent subvariety of ${\goth N}$ contains a non-nilpotent locally nilpotent subvariety?

b) The same problem for the variety of all pro-$p\hskip0.2ex $-groups (for a given prime $p$).
